diagnostic_evidence.quote: While SOBK samples pairs of mutually orthogonal blocks of contiguous rows, we propose to use the cumulative effective orthogonality of a block with \emph{all} other blocks in its random sampling, along with a dynamically aggregated block based on the current residue, for updating the iterative solution.

In \cref{algo:roar-bk}, when $\tilde{\lambda} $ is sufficiently small, updating the solution $x_t$ with respect to a block containing $\left\lfloor\frac{m}{k}\right\rfloor$ rows that contribute the most to the residual, reduces the upper and lower bounds of the error thus improving convergence in general.

We analyse the convergence properties of \Cref{algo:roar-bk}, and also we show that it can further decrease the residual encountered in SOBK, thereby accelerating convergence and improving the decay of relative residual norm (RRN)

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims a demonstration ("We show through \cref{thm:convergence_boost}") that the proposed additions — the cumulative-orthogonality sampling rule and the residual-based block — enhance convergence relative to SOBK. \cref{thm:convergence_boost} addresses only the residual-based block; no result in the paper analyzes the sampling distribution $\mathcal{P}$ or compares any error/residual quantity with SOBK's iterates. The promised theoretical comparison and the theoretical benefit of the orthogonality-based sampling therefore exceed the formal content.

failure_location.quote: We show through \cref{thm:convergence_boost} that this addition enhances the convergence of the earlier proposed SOBK method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the sentences to motivation/conjecture and restrict any claimed demonstration to the residual-based block, explicitly noting that the effect of the orthogonality sampling and the comparison with SOBK are empirical; supplying the missing demonstration would require a new convergence-comparison argument.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised theoretical justification for the orthogonality-based sampling and for superiority over SOBK is unsupported; the claimed comparison rests on experiments alone, and the companion claim that the paper shows a decreased residual relative to SOBK is equally unestablished.
issues.title: Claimed theoretical demonstration of improvement over SOBK is not provided
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of a claim of proof restores consistency between prose and formal content at negligible cost, but the promised theoretical comparison with SOBK (and for the sampling rule) is genuinely lost, so this is more than a minor fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: &=(\tilde{\lambda}I_r)^{-1}-(\tilde{\lambda}I_r)^{-1}M\{M^T (\tilde{\lambda}I_r)^{-1}M+(I_n)^{-1} \}M^T(\tilde{\lambda}I_r)^{-1}\notag\\
&=\frac{1}{\tilde{\lambda}}M^T-\frac{1}{\tilde{\lambda}^3}M^TM\{M^TM+\tilde{\lambda}I_n\}M^T\label{eq:wi3}
As R.H.S of \cref{eq:wi3}, and \cref{eq:wi4} are identical, the lemma holds.

issues.failure_explanation: The Woodbury step omits the inverse on the brace: the correct identity is $(\tilde\lambda I_r+MM^T)^{-1}=\tilde\lambda^{-1}I_r-\tilde\lambda^{-1}M(M^TM+\tilde\lambda I_n)^{-1}M^T$, whereas \eqref{eq:wi1} (and analogously \eqref{eq:wi2}) prints $\tilde\lambda^{-1}I_r-\tilde\lambda^{-3}M(M^TM+\tilde\lambda I_n)M^T$, which is not an identity. Hence \eqref{eq:wi3} and \eqref{eq:wi4} are not the LHS and RHS of \eqref{eq:woodberry_identity}, and their being "identical" proves nothing. Restoring the inverses makes the final comparison circular, since equating the corrected \eqref{eq:wi3} and \eqref{eq:wi4} is exactly the identity being proved. The lemma statement itself is true and follows from $(MM^T+\tilde\lambda I_r)M=M(M^TM+\tilde\lambda I_n)$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the derivation by the one-line argument: from $(MM^T+\tilde\lambda I_r)M=M(M^TM+\tilde\lambda I_n)$, multiply on the left by $(MM^T+\tilde\lambda I_r)^{-1}$ and on the right by $(M^TM+\tilde\lambda I_n)^{-1}$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of \cref{thm:woodberry_identity} is invalid as written. Because the lemma's statement is correct, the later uses of it (in \cref{thm:err_bound} and in the implementation notes) are not invalidated once a correct proof is supplied.
issues.title: Woodbury expansion in the proof of the push-through identity is a false matrix identity
issues.why_classification: A short, local replacement proof restores the (true) lemma and every guarantee that uses it, with no change to any statement, rate or scope.

&\le \frac{\tilde{\lambda}}{\lambda_{\min}^{+}(A_\tau^TA_\tau)+\tilde{\lambda}}\|x_t-x_\star\|_2\label{ew:errbound3}
The proposed method applies to the different types of linear systems, namely square ($m=n$), overdetermined ($m > n$), and underdetermined ($m < n$) cases.
obtain $k$ blocks $A_i$ and $b_i$, $i = 1,2,\ldots,k$

issues.failure_explanation: From \eqref{eq:errbound2}, $x_{t+1}-x_\star=\tilde\lambda(A_\tau^TA_\tau+\tilde\lambda I)^{-1}(x_t-x_\star)$, and this operator equals the identity on $\mathcal N(A_\tau)$; its 2-norm is $\tilde\lambda/(\lambda_{\min}(A_\tau^TA_\tau)+\tilde\lambda)$ where $\lambda_{\min}$ counts zero eigenvalues. Blocks contain $\lfloor m/k\rfloor$ rows, so $A_\tau^TA_\tau$ is singular whenever $\lfloor m/k\rfloor<n$ (in particular for every underdetermined system), and then the claimed factor $\tilde\lambda/(\lambda^+_{\min}+\tilde\lambda)<1$ is false. Counterexample: $A=I_2$, $b=(1,1)^T$, block $A_1=(1,0)$, $x_t=(1,2)^T$: the block residual is zero, so $x_{t+1}=x_t$ and $\|x_{t+1}-x_\star\|=1$, contradicting $\le\frac{\tilde\lambda}{1+\tilde\lambda}\cdot 1$. The same mechanism (non-contraction of components in $\mathcal N(A_\tau)$, and of $x_0-x_\star$ components in $\mathcal N(A)$) also destroys the geometric rate in the "Equivalently" clause.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that every block (including the residual block $A_{\mathcal I}$) has full column rank, so that $\lambda^+_{\min}=\lambda_{\min}>0$; retaining the advertised underdetermined and $\lfloor m/k\rfloor<n$ regimes requires replacing the per-step contraction by a joint-block argument in which null directions are contracted only by later blocks.
issues.overall_effect: The per-step contraction and the geometric expected-error rate of \cref{thm:err_bound} are unreliable in the paper's standard regime (blocks with fewer rows than columns), i.e. for tall and underdetermined systems and for the $k\approx\sqrt m$ block sizes used in the experiments; the paper's advertised "convergence analysis of the proposed method" is lost there.
issues.title: Contraction factor uses the smallest nonzero eigenvalue although the update is the identity on the block's null space
issues.why_classification: The cheap repair (full-column-rank blocks) excludes the advertised underdetermined regime and essentially all experimental configurations with $\lfloor m/k\rfloor<n$, while any repair keeping those regimes needs a new joint-block analysis and a different (mean rather than per-step geometric) guarantee; no comparable version of the stated rate survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $x_\star$ be $A^\dagger b$.
For linear least-squares problems, the randomized block-Kaczmarz (RBK) method exemplifies such an approach
x^{(\mu)}=\text{arg}\text{min}_{x\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times 1}} \|Ax-b\|_{\bar{W}}^2, \text {and} \quad r^{(\mu)}=b-Ax^{(\mu)}
Then the expectation of the ROR-BK iterates $x_T$ converges to $x^{(\mu)}$ as

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed step replaces $b_\tau-A_\tau x_t$ by $-A_\tau(x_t-x_\star)$, which requires $b_\tau=A_\tau x_\star$; the theorem states no such hypothesis while the paper explicitly covers linear least-squares problems. There $b_\tau-A_\tau x_\star\ne0$ and the recursion acquires the additive term $A_\tau^T(A_\tau A_\tau^T+\tilde\lambda I)^{-1}(b_\tau-A_\tau x_\star)$, so $x_\star=A^\dagger b$ is not a fixed point. E.g. $A=(1,1)^T$, $b=(0,1)^T$, blocks = the two rows, $x_\star=1/2$, $x_t=x_\star$: the first-row update gives $x_{t+1}=\frac{\tilde\lambda}{1+\tilde\lambda}\cdot\frac12\ne x_\star$, contradicting $\|x_{t+1}-x_\star\|\le\frac{\tilde\lambda}{1+\tilde\lambda}\|x_t-x_\star\|=0$. This also conflicts with \cref{thm:dobk_for_least_square_problems}, where the limit is $x^{(\mu)}$, not $A^\dagger b$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and use the hypothesis $b\in\mathcal R(A)$ (equivalently $b_\tau=A_\tau x_\star$ for every block); for inconsistent right-hand sides the claim must be reformulated with the limit point $x^{(\mu)}$ and a mean, not pathwise, guarantee as in \cref{thm:dobk_for_least_square_problems}.
issues.overall_effect: For inconsistent right-hand sides (the least-squares problems the abstract and the least-squares discussion advertise), the claimed contraction to $x_\star=A^\dagger b$ and its rate are unreliable; the analogous approximation step of \cref{thm:convergence_boost} fails for the same reason.
issues.title: Error recursion silently assumes a consistent right-hand side although least-squares problems are covered
issues.why_classification: Adding the consistency hypothesis is a short local repair that preserves the statement, its rate and the whole consistent-system scope, but it withdraws the geometric guarantee for the advertised least-squares regime, leaving only the weaker mean-convergence result; that is a limited but real loss, not a minor edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \|x_t-x_\star\|_2^2-\frac{\|A_\tau x_t-b\|_2^{2}}{\lambda_{\min}^{+}(A_\tau^{T}A_\tau)}\lesssim \|x_{t+1}-x_\star\|_2^2 & \lesssim \|x_t-x_\star\|_2^2-\frac{\|A_\tau x_t-b\|_2^{2}}{\lambda_{\max}^{+}(A_\tau^{T}A_\tau)}\label{eq:errbound5}
where, $\lambda_{\min}^{+}(A_\tau^T A_\tau), \lambda_{\max}^{+}(A_\tau^TA_\tau)$ are the smallest and largest non-zero eigenvalues of $A_\tau^T A_\tau$ respectively.

In step:\ref{step:roar-bk} of \cref{algo:roar-bk}, we use the squared elements of the residue vector $r$ and construct the set of indices $\mathcal{I}$, representing the required $\lfloor \frac{m}{k}\rfloor$ rows, to minimize the 2-norm of the current residue $\|b-Ax_{j}\|_2^2$ in each update of the solution.

issues.failure_explanation: Both bounds in \eqref{eq:errbound5} contain the factors $\lambda^+_{\max}(A_S^TA_S)$ and $\lambda^+_{\min}(A_S^TA_S)$, which vary with the candidate row set $S$; being "bounded for a given system" does not make them constant across $S$, so maximizing $\|A_Sx_t-b_S\|_2^2$ minimizes neither bound. Concrete counterexample: rows $a_1=(10^3,0)$ with $b_1=10^2$ and $a_2=(0,1)$ with $b_2=50$, $x_t=0$ and $\lfloor m/k\rfloor=1$. The largest-residual set $\{1\}$ improves the upper-bound term by $10^4/10^6=10^{-2}$ only, while $\{2\}$ improves it by $2500/1=2500$; the error falls from $\approx50.0001$ to $50$ with $\{1\}$ but to $0.1$ with $\{2\}$. Hence the conclusion, and the parallel claim that the chosen rows "minimize the 2-norm of the current residue", are false in general (and the bounds themselves hold only up to $\approx$, since $\tilde\lambda$ is only "sufficiently small").

failure_location.quote: we minimize the above upper and lower bounds of the error $\|x_{t+1}-x_\star\|_2^2$ in \cref{eq:errbound5}, as $\lambda_{\min}^{+}, \lambda_{\min}^{-}$ are bounded for a given system, and thus ensure faster convergence in general over many iterations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the result to claim only that the greedy choice maximizes the residual term $\|A_Sx_t-b_S\|_2^2$ appearing in the bounds, with improvement of the bounds when the spectral factors are comparable across candidate sets (e.g. uniformly scaled rows); alternatively change the selection rule to maximize $\|A_Sx_t-b_S\|_2^2/\lambda^+_{\max}(A_S^TA_S)$ and repeat the comparison.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's claim that residual-greedy aggregation improves convergence is unreliable, and with it the theoretical support for the residue-based ingredient of ROR-BK and the statement that the selected rows minimize $\|b-Ax_j\|_2$.
issues.title: Residual-greedy block selection does not minimize the error bounds, whose spectral factors depend on the chosen rows
issues.why_classification: The statement must be weakened or the selection rule changed and re-compared, so more than a local fix is needed, but a recognizable result about the residual term survives without any new global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $z_0$ (the initial solution with which ROR-BK as an inner-iteration starts) and $x_0 \in \mathcal{R}(A^{T})$, FABGMRES with an inner iteration of ROR-BK (\cref{algo:fabgmres_dobk}) gives a solution $x_k \in \mathcal{R}(A^T)$ minimizing $\norm{b-Ax_k}_2$.
$y_k = \arg\min_{y \in \mathbb{R}^k} \|\beta e_1 - \tilde{H}_k y\|_2$
$x_\star$ denotes the minimum residual-norm solution of \cref{eq:linear_system}.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership $x_k\in\mathcal R(A^T)$ (i.e. $x_k\perp\mathcal N(A)$) implies only that $x_k$ is the minimum-Euclidean-norm vector among vectors with the same image $Ax_k$; it does not imply that $\|b-Ax_k\|_2$ is minimal. The least-squares step of \cref{algo:fabgmres_dobk} minimizes $\|\beta e_1-\tilde H_ky\|_2=\min_{u\in\mathrm{span}\{z_1,\dots,z_k\}}\|b-A(x_0+u)\|_2$, i.e. only over the constructed subspace, and at finite iterations the returned $x_k$ is not a solution of $Ax=b$ at all. The conclusion drawn (minimum residual / "the minimum residual-norm solution", which the notation identifies with $A^\dagger b$) is therefore a materially different claim from what the argument establishes.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, when $x_k$ is an approximate solution of \eqref{eq:linear_system} obtained through \cref{algo:fabgmres_dobk}, it is the minimum residual-norm solution, since $x_k \in \mathcal{R}(A^T) \perp \mathcal{N}(A)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the remark accordingly: $x_k\in\mathcal R(A^T)$ and minimizes $\|b-Ax\|_2$ over $x_0+\mathrm{span}\{z_1,\dots,z_k\}$; and if $x_k$ is an exact least-squares solution it is the minimum-norm one, $A^\dagger b$.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee attached to \cref{algo:fabgmres_dobk} is unreliable: one obtains at most $x_k\in\mathcal R(A^T)$ (hence minimum $\|x\|$ among vectors with the same residual) and residual minimization over $x_0+\mathrm{span}\{z_1,\dots,z_k\}$, not residual minimality or equality with $A^\dagger b$.
issues.title: FAB-GMRES output claimed to minimize the residual although the proof establishes only the range/minimum-norm property
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws a promised guarantee (minimality of the residual) as stated, so it cannot be minor, but it is a short statement change that preserves the minimum-norm property and the standard GMRES guarantee, leaving a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \bar{W}=\mathbb{E}_{S \sim \mu}[W(S)], \text{and} \quad \bar{P}=  \mathbb{E}_{S\sim \mu}[P(S)]
Sample an index $\tau$ w.r.t the probability distribution $\mathcal{P}$.
$r = b - A x_{j}$ and pick indices $\mathcal{I}$ of top $\left\lfloor \frac{m}{k} \right\rfloor$ squared elements $r_i^2$ where $i=1,2,\dots m$
The proof follows from the Theorem 4.1 in \cite{ReRBK}.

issues.failure_explanation: The objects $\bar W=\mathbb E_{S\sim\mu}W(S)$, $\bar P=\mathbb E_{S\sim\mu}P(S)$ and the rate require every update to be an independent draw from a fixed distribution $\mu$, since only then does one get $\mathbb E[x_{t+1}\mid x_t]=x_t-\bar P(x_t-x^{(\mu)})$ (using $A^T\bar W(b-Ax^{(\mu)})=0$). \cref{algo:roar-bk} performs three draws from $\mathcal P$ and one update on the set $\mathcal I$ of the largest current residuals, which is a function of $x_j$ and hence not a $\mu$-draw; its drift does not vanish at $x^{(\mu)}$. Example: rows $(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)$ of $A$, $b=(0,0,1)^T$, three one-row blocks, $\tilde\lambda\to0$: the theorem's bound at $T=1$ with $x_0=x^{(\mu)}=(0.128,0.128)$ forces $\mathbb E[x_1]=x^{(\mu)}$, but enumerating the 27 sampling sequences shows the extra largest-residual update has strictly positive expected drift (sum coordinate between $0.50$ and $0.58$), so $\mathbb E[x_1]\ne x^{(\mu)}$. The one-line proof does not check any hypothesis of the cited result. In addition, $x^{(\mu)}$ is defined as "$\arg\min$", which is set-valued when $A$ is rank deficient, so the bound is ill-defined unless the minimum-norm minimizer is selected.

failure_location.quote: \textit{Consider the ROR-BK algorithm, namely \cref{algo:roar-bk} with $M(A_S) = (A_S A_S^\top + \tilde{\lambda} I)^{-1}$ and $\mu$ be the sampling rule defined earlier.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the theorem to the sub-iteration consisting only of $\mu$-sampled block updates (i.e. drop the largest-residual update from the analyzed scheme) and define $x^{(\mu)}$ as the minimum-norm $\bar W$-least-squares minimizer; covering the full \cref{algo:roar-bk} iteration requires a new analysis of iterate-dependent sampling.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed mean convergence and rate of the ROR-BK iterates to the weighted least-squares solution $x^{(\mu)}$ are unreliable; the statement that this method "can also solve a weighted least square solution ... with the required convergence properties" and the paper's least-squares guarantee lose their support.
issues.title: Weighted least-squares convergence theorem applied to iterate-adaptive blocks that are not draws from the sampling law
issues.why_classification: Narrowing the statement to the sampled updates is a limited weakening that leaves a recognizable mean-convergence result, but the guarantee for the full algorithm (with the residual-based block) is lost and cannot be recovered without a new argument.
